sources.note: Nothing for Abai Sungai: it appears only as the map key 'SgAb = Abai Sungai' (Map 11.1 key, p. 370) and in a footnote distinguishing it from the Murutic Abai Sembuak/Abai Tubu ('These two languages should not be confused with Abai Sungai, a Paitanic language spoken in eastern Sabah.. spoken by a tribe called "Sungai" located in the town of Abai'). Sec. 11.4.7 'Paitanic' (p. 399) discusses subgrouping only. The only stress remarks are about Philippine languages (sec. 8.2.9) and a Blust quote on schwa.

sources.citation: King, Julie K. & John Wayne King (eds.). 1984. Languages of Sabah: A survey report. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. Ch. 2 (Kenneth D. Smith, 'The languages of Sabah: a tentative lexicostatistical classification'), sec. 2.3.9.2.3 'Abai Sungai language', p. 18; ch. 3 (Julie K. King, 'The Paitanic language family', pp. 139-153), sec. 3.3 'Abai Sungai language', pp. 147-148.
sources.note: Nothing. Abai Sungai is treated only lexicostatistically (p. 18: closest relation 80 PSC with Sinarupa/Bulot and Kuamut dialects of Upper Kinabatangan) and by intelligibility testing at Abai KN (pp. 147-148: 'The only village tested where the Abai Sungai language is spoken was the village of Abai KN.. test results were low in all cases'). The strings stress/accent/penult occur nowhere in the 368-page volume.
